newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka troops resume campaign to capture highway.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka troops resume campaign to capture highway.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops on Tuesday resumed their campaign to capture a vital highway in northern territory held by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, military officials said.

Infantry soldiers supported by planes, helicopter gunships, tanks and artillery began moving forward from earlier held positions north of Vavuniya, which lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.

Details of the military's advance were not immediately available, but the troops launched the campaign in May to capture the 88 km (55 mile) highway that links the government-held town of Vavuniya to Kilinochchi.
The government is seeking to capture the highway to ensure a land route to the Jaffna peninsula, where more than half a million Tamils live. At present all supplies are taken to Jaffna by sea or air.
On August 7, two divisions of troops linked up south of Puliyankulam town, 22 km (14 miles) north of Vavuniya.
One division of troops had moved northwards from Vavuniya, while the other from northeastern Nedunkeni.
The operation "Jaya Sikuru" (Sure of Victory) had slowed down after three rebel counterattacks in which socres of rebels and soldiers were killed.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east in a war which began in 1983. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed, but LTTE say the is toll higher.
